wp2_readout_baseline_addendum.what: Added the calibrated readout-error-mitigation baseline 'linv_calib' (method code in code/vaqem_methods.py: calib_train_indices, calib_pairs, flip_rate_residual, fit_flip_rate, mitigator_linv_calib; wired into run_experiments.all_methods).
wp2_readout_baseline_addendum.why_e2_e3_e5_rerun: all_methods() is called by exp_sweep (E2) and exp_calib (E5), so those two were regenerated; E3 was regenerated as a determinism control and came out byte-identical (exp_shots does not call all_methods and carries no linv_calib rows).
wp2_readout_baseline_addendum.acceptance_e2: final_sweep.json 992 -> 1056 rows: 64 added, all method 'linv_calib' (16 settings x 4 shot budgets); 0 removed; 0 changed. Every pre-existing number is byte-identical to the pre-WP2 archive.
wp2_readout_baseline_addendum.acceptance_e5: e5_calib.json 288 -> 306 rows: 18 added, all 'linv_calib'; 0 removed; the 288 shared rows differ only in the wall-clock fields t_fit_s/t_retrain_s, no scientific field changed.
wp2_readout_baseline_addendum.why_e4_not_rerun: e4_scaling.json carries the cold-cache wall-clock measurements t_data_s/t_oracle_s that paper/check_tex.py:check_costs audits, and that check deliberately FAILS when the scaling rows report data_from_cache. A warm-cache re-run would replace a simulation cost with a cache-lookup time, and splicing freshly timed linv_calib rows into the archived file would mix two cache provenances inside one file. E4 therefore keeps its archived contents and has no linv_calib rows; the readout baseline is compared in E2, E3 and E5, where provenance is uniform.
wp2_readout_baseline_addendum.environment_note: autograd must be >= 1.9: vaqem_lib.gate_real_block uses plain-numpy cos/sin so that autograd.grad can differentiate the statevector simulation, which needs ArrayBox.__array_ufunc__ (absent in 1.8.0). See requirements.txt.
wp2_readout_baseline_addendum.stability_note: run_experiments.py sweep was observed to die with an intermittent SIGSEGV at a varying setting when the machine was near memory exhaustion (1-3 GB free, no swap), including once at the default --workers=cpu_count-2=22. It is not reproducible at --workers 6 with the paper parameters (two full 16-setting runs completed, 361.0 s and 5.9 min). The sweep writes its JSON after every setting, so a crash loses only the in-flight setting.

e6_pec_baseline_addendum.what: Added a probabilistic-error-cancellation (PEC) readout baseline (code/vaqem_methods.py: pec_gamma, pec_sector_matrix, pec_sample, mitigator_pec, mitigator_pec_known, pec_mismatch_bias; new self-test code/test_pec.py) and a dedicated experiment exp_pec (E6) in code/run_experiments.py, selectable as 'pec'.
e6_pec_baseline_addendum.why_correct: PEC is built as the exact quasi-probability inverse of the same binomial sector channel that linv_calib inverts: corrections are drawn per observed bitstring with probability |c1|/(|c0|+|c1|) = q and reweighted by gamma*(-1)^(#corrections). Because the net sector shift depends only on the observed sector, PEC is exactly representable on the (N+1)-dimensional sector distribution. test_pec.py proves its expected transition matrix M equals K_m^-T to 1.55e-15 over N in {1,2,4,8}, q in {0.01,0.03,0.05}, that sum_a'|M[a,a']| = gamma for every sector, that the per-shot sampler is unbiased, and that its per-trial spread matches the analytic gamma-inflated sd (observed 0.1317 vs analytic 0.1311).
e6_pec_baseline_addendum.why_separate_file: At infinite shots PEC is provably the SAME estimator as the deterministic inverse, so adding pec_* rows to final_sweep.json would duplicate the archived linv_* rows (62k lines) without adding information. E6 therefore lives in results/e6_pec.json and is self-contained for the PEC-vs-inverse comparison: it recomputes 'none' and 'linv_calib' on the same settings and shot budgets. No comparator is joined from final_sweep.json: 'none', 'linv_calib', 'pec_calib' and 'pec_known' are all recomputed inside E6 on one shared grid and sampler seed, so every PEC contrast is paired within the file. (An earlier revision of this note claimed the D-VAQEM comparator was joined from final_sweep.json and justified that by identical parameters; both halves were wrong -- see parameters_identical_to_e2_correction. Because the grids differ, the absolute dB levels in e6_pec.json are NOT comparable to the E2 tables, and code/bootstrap_ci.build_pec / collect_numbers.sec_e6 deliberately never read final_sweep.json.)
e6_pec_baseline_addendum.why_isolated_exp_root: run_experiments.main() writes run_manifest.json unconditionally, so E6 was run with --exp-root <tmp> and results/e6_pec.json copied in by hand. This file, including wp2_readout_baseline_addendum, was therefore never overwritten by the E6 run.
e6_pec_baseline_addendum.command: OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 python run_experiments.py pec --workers 6 --exp-root <tmp>   # then cp <tmp>/e6_pec.json results/
e6_pec_baseline_addendum.acceptance: e6_pec.json: 620 rows over 20 settings = the 16 archived E2 settings plus 4 stress settings (readout_0.10/0.15/0.20 and depol_0.01_readout_0.03) that probe the regime where the quasi-probability overhead bites. Three axes: 'overhead' (gamma, gamma^2 per setting), 'budget' (none / linv_calib / pec_calib / pec_known at inf,S256,S1024,S4096), 'mismatch' (pec_calib / linv_calib at 7 assumed rates plus the unmitigated reference). Runtime 550 s.

key_findings.gamma_range_paper_grid: gamma = (1-2q_hat)^-N spans 1.18 (readout_0.01) to 5.44e10 (deph_0.05, q_hat = 0.477) across the 16 archived settings, i.e. a variance amplification gamma^2 of up to 2.96e21 (214.7 dB) on an ARCHIVED setting, not only on a stress one. The 4 stress settings add gamma^2 up to 8654 (depol_0.01_readout_0.03, q_hat = 0.216), which is far below the deph_0.05 figure; an earlier revision of this note implied the stress settings were the extreme.
key_findings.finite_shot_penalty: PEC never beats the deterministic inverse in any setting at any budget (0/16 at each of S256, S1024, S4096); its MSE is 1.01x-13.4x larger. The ratio is meaningless where both fail, so the robust statement is the win count, not the median.
key_findings.worse_than_none: PEC is worse than no mitigation at all in 18 of 64 paper-grid cells, versus 4 of 64 for linv_calib, and every one of those is a high-gamma channel.
key_findings.model_mismatch: A rate error of only 0.005 degrades PEC/linv by roughly 600x on the pure readout settings (readout_0.02: 3.20e-07 -> 1.60e-04 at infinite shots) and the error saturates at a bias floor that more shots cannot remove. D-VAQEM has no assumed rate, so it has no such floor.
key_findings.regularisation_note: linv_calib applies a Tikhonov-regularised inverse (alpha=1e-6) while PEC applies the exact one. They agree to 2e-6..1e-2 relative on well-conditioned channels (q_hat <= 0.15) and diverge up to 6.8x on near-singular ones (deph_0.05, q_hat = 0.477), where the regularisation is what keeps linv finite.

e6_pec_baseline_addendum.environment_note: Same as wp2_readout_baseline_addendum: autograd >= 1.9, .venv-pl, numpy 2.2.6, python 3.11.15, 24 CPUs.

E6 ran at n_cal=25, n_tst=41, n_trials=25 (the exp_pec defaults); the archived E2/E3/E5 headline run used n_cal=21, n_tst=21, n_trials=41 (run_manifest n_cal/n_tst/n_trials). Verified against the data, not just the CLI record: len(err2) is 41 in every e6_pec.json row that carries per-phase errors and 21 in every final_sweep.json row, and the stored n_trials is 25 vs 41. N=8, seed=0 and shots_list=(256,1024,4096) DO match.
